incidents.title: ICE Agents Leave "Death Cards" in Vehicles of Detained; DHS Investigating
incidents.summary: ICE agents detained nine individuals in Eagle County - eight during what advocates called "fake traffic stops" and one while walking to a bus stop. Agents left ace of spades playing cards (bearing "ICE Denver Field Office" text) inside at least two vehicles of detained individuals. The ace of spades has historical associations with racism and death dating to the Vietnam War. DHS announced an investigation and "unequivocally condemns this type of action and/or officer conduct." Voces Unidas called it "psychological harassment."

incidents.title: DHS Statement: Denver Arrest of Mexican National
incidents.summary: DHS announced the arrest of Carlos Chavez-Salas, a Mexican national, in Denver. ICE cited a prior conviction for "menacing" as justification for the arrest.

incidents.title: DHS Statement: Grand Junction Arrest of Honduran National
incidents.summary: DHS announced the arrest of Nerlin Jhonatan Perez-Amaya, a Honduran national, in Grand Junction. ICE cited a prior conviction for "unlawful electronic sexual communication" as justification for the arrest.

incidents.title: 1,000 Protest in Denver After ICE Kills Colorado Springs Native in Minneapolis
incidents.summary: About 1,000 people gathered at the Colorado State Capitol and marched through downtown Denver to protest the fatal ICE shooting of Renee Nicole Good in Minneapolis. Good, 37, was born and raised in Colorado Springs and was shot in the head through her car window by an ICE agent on January 7, 2026 during an immigration operation. She was a U.S. citizen with no connection to the ICE target. Governor Jared Polis called the shooting "deeply disturbing."
incidents.location: Colorado State Capitol and downtown Denver

incidents.title: ICE Arrests Alleged Tren de Aragua Member Wanted for Murder in New Mexico
incidents.summary: ICE Homeland Security Investigations arrested Yorvis Michel Carrascal Campo, a Venezuelan national and alleged member of the Tren de Aragua gang, in Colorado Springs. He was wanted in New Mexico for murder, racketeering, and drug trafficking in connection with a June 2024 kidnapping and murder.

incidents.title: ICE Agents Impersonate Store Employees in Colorado Springs; Detentions at Walmart
incidents.summary: ICE agents in Colorado Springs were documented impersonating King Soopers and 7-Eleven employees to approach individuals. On December 7, video was posted showing ICE detaining individuals outside a Walmart on Murray Boulevard. The Colorado Immigrant Rights Coalition documented escalating tactics in the area, including use of Automatic License Plate Reader (ALPR) surveillance to locate individuals. Community members organized volunteer networks to canvass neighborhoods and distribute multilingual materials in response.

incidents.title: ICE Awards $39 Million Contract for New Colorado Detention Facility in Hudson
incidents.summary: ICE awarded GEO Group a $39 million contract to operate the former Hudson Correctional Facility (now called "Big Horn Correctional Facility") as an immigration detention center. The facility, dormant since 2014, has capacity for 1,256 beds. This is part of a plan to triple ICE detention capacity in Colorado. The town council was not approached by GEO Group or ICE before the plans were announced. Community protests were held at the site.
incidents.latestUpdate: [Hundreds protest at facility site](https://www.denverpost.com/2026/01/21/hudson-correctional-facility-colorado-ice-detention/) demanding it not be used for ICE detention.

incidents.title: Federal Judge Rules ICE Conduct in Colorado "Unlawful"
incidents.summary: U.S. District Judge R. Brooke Jackson issued a 66-page preliminary injunction ruling that ICE has "routinely" made unlawful warrantless arrests in Colorado. The ruling restricts how immigration officers can arrest people in the state and requires documentation of flight risk assessments before any warrantless arrest. The case was certified as a class action covering all people arrested since January 20, 2025.
incidents.latestUpdate: ICE announced [appeal to 10th Circuit Court of Appeals](https://www.gjsentinel.com/news/western_colorado/ice-to-appeal-judges-ruling-requiring-agents-to-follow-laws-during-arrests/article_5c25e1b9-01d5-4b4a-96ab-459cf1414992.html).

incidents.title: Member of Historic Pueblo Family Arrested at Courthouse, Self-Deports
incidents.summary: Jose Guadalupe Alejo Lamberto, husband of Cristiana Alejo Lamberto (a member of the historic Autobee family prominent in Pueblo since the 1840s), was arrested by ICE outside the El Paso County Courthouse after his initial appearance for a DUI case. When his wife filmed the encounter and asked to see a warrant, an ICE agent stated they were "authorized to make warrantless arrests." The situation escalated when Cristiana called her mother to pick up her daughter. ICE broke the truck window and removed Jose. He paid $400 and signed an agreement to self-deport on November 11, 2025 - his 7th wedding anniversary.
incidents.location: El Paso County Courthouse parking lot

incidents.title: ICE Conducts Operation in Montrose; Woman Detained, Vehicle Abandoned
incidents.summary: ICE conducted an operation in Montrose, arresting a woman and taking away vehicle passengers from a gravel lot near Pomona Brewing and Velocity Car Wash on the north side of town. A Chevrolet truck was left abandoned in the gravel lot. Federal ICE agents were on scene along with a Montrose police officer.

incidents.title: Father and Two Children Detained En Route to School; ICE Admits Wrong Person; Protesters Pepper-Sprayed
incidents.summary: ICE agents detained Fernando Jaramillo-Solano, a Colombian father with an active asylum case, and his two children (ages 12 and 15) at approximately 7:30 a.m. while they were driving to school. ICE's third-ranking Denver official later testified that "the father was mistaken for somebody else" but agents arrested all three anyway without warrants. A 57-year-old woman was thrown to the ground by a masked agent when she tried to retrieve her phone while filming a protest later in the day. Hundreds of protesters formed a human chain outside the ICE field office for over 24 hours. Federal agents used pepper spray and rubber bullets on protesters. The Colorado Bureau of Investigation opened an investigation. The family was transferred to a detention center in Dilley, Texas, and eventually agreed to leave the U.S. due to trauma experienced in detention.

incidents.title: Fifth Grade Teacher Detained with Family at Routine Immigration Appointment
incidents.summary: Marina Ortiz, a fifth-grade teacher at Global Village Academy in Parker (Douglas County), was detained along with her family while attending a routine immigration appointment at the ICE field office in Centennial. The school confirmed she had a valid employment authorization document through 2029. ICE stated she entered the country illegally in 2022. She and her family were sent to a detention center in Dilley, Texas, and eventually agreed to voluntarily depart to Peru in November 2025.

incidents.title: First ICE Visit to Telluride Residence Results in Unrelated Arrest
incidents.summary: ICE agents went to a residence at the Shandoka apartment complex in Telluride looking for a specific individual. When they didn't find that person, they made an apparently unrelated arrest of a man on nearby streets, taking him to the ICE facility in Durango. This was the first time ICE had come to a Telluride residence looking for someone. The Telluride Marshal's office was not notified before or after the operation.

incidents.title: County Commissioner "Boxed In" by ICE Agents After Filming Operations
incidents.summary: Routt County Commissioner Angelica Salinas reported that ICE officers "boxed in" her vehicle at the Oak Creek post office after she took video of their operations. She stated the officers "took off" when they saw her husband. ICE called her account a "blatant and pathetic lie" and released a photo from an agent's vehicle. Salinas stood by her account. The incident occurred amid increased ICE activity in Steamboat Springs and Oak Creek.

incidents.title: ICE Draws Gun, Smashes Car Window with 1-Month-Old Baby Inside
incidents.summary: Jose de Jesus Aguilera-Bautista was driving with his partner Maya England and their 1-month-old son when three unmarked ICE SUVs followed them after he left an Alamosa County courthouse DUI hearing. Vehicles boxed them in at an intersection. An ICE agent exited with weapon drawn, pointing it at Aguilera through the windshield. A second agent smashed the car window with a baton while England screamed "We have a baby!" Glass scattered into the vehicle where the infant was seated. Aguilera was handcuffed without resistance and eventually deported to Mexico.

incidents.title: ICE Raids Frisco Restaurant; 10 Detained Across Summit County; School Attendance Drops 35%
incidents.summary: Federal agents from ICE Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) and Enforcement and Removal Operations (ERO) executed a search warrant at Hacienda Real, a Mexican restaurant in Frisco, following an anonymous tip about undocumented workers. Two workers (a cook and a waiter) were detained and taken to the Aurora detention center. Agents also executed a warrant at a home in Dillon Valley and seized computer towers and employee records. The restaurant was forced to close. Over the following days, at least 8 more people were detained in the area through traffic stops near the Super 8 hotel and Shell gas station and at a construction site, bringing the total to 10 detained by September 26. Summit School District saw a 35% attendance drop lasting two weeks.
incidents.location: Hacienda Real restaurant and Dillon Valley residence

incidents.title: ICE Enters Winter Park McDonald's; Legal Worker Questioned, Undocumented Man Arrested
incidents.summary: ICE agents entered a McDonald's restaurant in Winter Park, detained and questioned manager Justin Ramirez, who holds a legal U.S. work permit and was later released. Agents then arrested Evin Gonzales, an undocumented Nicaraguan man from nearby Fraser who had previously worked at the restaurant. Gonzales had no known criminal record. This was the first confirmed ICE activity in Grand County.

incidents.title: Mother Arrested at Courthouse; ICE Orders Family to Bring 7-Year-Old for Detention
incidents.summary: Carolina Suarez Estrada, a 33-year-old asylum seeker with a valid work permit, was arrested inside the Chaffee County court complex while ICE officers were conducting operations in Salida. ICE agents then demanded the family bring her 7-year-old son Luciano to meet her; the child was detained separately in Alamosa. The family had work permits, legal employment at a construction company, and were lawfully present in the U.S. with their asylum case pending. Mother and child were held at the South Texas Family Residential Center in Dilley, Texas for nearly a month before being released September 15, 2025.

incidents.title: Judge Bars ICE Civil Arrests at San Luis Valley Courthouses
incidents.summary: 12th Judicial District Chief Judge Amanda C. Hopkins issued an administrative order barring civil ICE arrests in courthouses across six San Luis Valley counties: Alamosa, Conejos, Costilla, Saguache, Mineral, and Rio Grande. The order stated that civil arrests "have a chilling effect not only on criminal defendants' presence at their hearings, but also on victims reporting crimes." This followed the earlier Western Slope courthouse order issued in April.

incidents.title: ICE Agent Fires 3 Shots at Vehicle During Black Forest Raid
incidents.summary: ICE agents raided the Timber Ridge housing development construction site in Black Forest, north of Colorado Springs, seeking two fugitives. When suspects allegedly attempted to drive into a federal agent, an ICE officer fired three shots at the vehicle. No injuries were reported. One suspect was arrested; the other (Jose Mendez-Chavez) remained at large for months. The El Paso County Sheriff's Office issued a shelter-in-place order during the operation. Construction workers from multiple job sites fled when ICE arrived. Activists disputed claims that the men tried to ram ICE vehicles.
incidents.location: Timber Ridge housing development, Burgess Road

incidents.title: ICE Arrests 243 People in 9-Day Denver Metro Operation
incidents.summary: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement conducted a 9-day enforcement operation across the Denver metro area from July 12-20, 2025, arresting 243 people. ICE claimed all those arrested were charged with or convicted of criminal offenses, though critics noted the operation reflected a significant escalation of arrests in Colorado, with the state seeing more than 17 arrests per day during this period.

incidents.title: Father of Five Deported Without Hearing; Daughter Has Leukemia
incidents.summary: A Mexican father of five who had worked in the Uncompahgre Valley farm fields was detained by ICE while on his way to work. He was quickly deported without a hearing. He had three minor traffic offenses and was driving without a license. His U.S. citizen daughter reportedly has leukemia and he had been driving her to Denver for treatment. The deportation left the family without a primary caregiver for the sick child.

incidents.title: Two Construction Workers Detained En Route to Job Site
incidents.summary: Two people driving east from Durango to a construction site in Pagosa Springs were stopped and detained by ICE. The workers were traveling to their job when they were intercepted. This incident was documented by the local advocacy group Compañeros.

incidents.title: ICE Operation in Longmont; Rapid Response Network Responds; No Arrests Made
incidents.summary: ICE conducted an operation in a Longmont neighborhood seeking Jose Reyes Leon-Deras, an El Salvadoran national wanted for child rape in Italy. Colorado Rapid Response Network volunteers responded to the scene. ICE alleged volunteers "alerted the suspect and allowed him to escape" using a bullhorn to share rights information. The Rapid Response Network denied obstruction, stating volunteers only documented and informed people of their rights. ICE left the neighborhood at 8:28 a.m. with no one detained. Longmont Public Safety stated the FBI was also present for a "criminal matter not related to immigration status."

incidents.title: Man Violently Arrested at Federal Courthouse as Child Watches; Legal Observer Detained
incidents.summary: At the Byron Rogers Federal Building in Denver, a man was arrested "very roughly, very violently" inside the federal courthouse bathroom while his child watched, trembling and in tears. Additionally, a legal observer from the American Friends Service Committee was detained, handcuffed, and cited while observing court proceedings. The observer's charges were later dropped.

incidents.title: 18 Protesters Arrested at "ICE Out!" Demonstration at State Capitol
incidents.summary: Thousands gathered at the Colorado State Capitol to protest ICE enforcement in solidarity with Los Angeles anti-ICE protests. Police deployed smoke grenades and pepper balls to disperse crowds. Eighteen people were arrested on various charges including obstructing streets, assault on police officers, graffiti, and interference with police authority. The protests were organized by Denver Party for Socialism and Liberation and the Colorado Immigrant Rights Coalition.

incidents.title: College Student Detained After Deputy Shares Info with ICE via Signal
incidents.summary: Caroline Dias Goncalves, a 19-year-old University of Utah nursing student from Brazil, was pulled over by Mesa County Deputy Alexander Zwinck for following a semi-truck too closely. During the 19-minute stop, the deputy asked about her accent and origins. After she disclosed being born in Brazil, the deputy uploaded her information to a Signal group chat called "GJ Highway Hitters" that included federal immigration officers. ICE agents stopped her a few miles down the road and detained her for 15 days at the Aurora facility. Her case became part of a landmark ACLU lawsuit.

incidents.title: ICE Detains Individual with Outstanding Warrant Near Carbondale
incidents.summary: ICE agents detained an individual with an outstanding warrant near Carbondale. On the same day, Voces Unidas reported two additional ICE appearances in Glenwood Springs and one on I-70 between Glenwood and Rifle, indicating coordinated activity across Garfield County.

incidents.title: Father of Four Detained for Wrong Person, Held 90+ Days
incidents.summary: Refugio Ramirez Ovando, a 43-year-old father of four U.S. citizen children who had lived in Colorado for 20 years, was pulled over by ICE agents in unmarked cars while driving to his Grand Junction construction job where he had worked for 18 years. An ICE agent later admitted they had been looking for someone else and arrested him by mistake. He was held at the Aurora detention facility for more than 90 days. His case became part of a landmark ACLU lawsuit that resulted in a federal judge ruling ICE's conduct in Colorado was "unlawful."

incidents.title: ICE Raids Durango Granite Business, Detains 5 Workers
incidents.summary: About 10 ICE and Homeland Security Investigations agents in five vehicles arrived at Rock Solid Custom Granite in Durango and arrested five employees who allegedly lacked "proper documentation." This was the first "real raid" in Durango since Trump's second term began, according to local advocacy group Compañeros. The business manager described the arrested workers as "non-criminals" and said his staff was reduced to just four people.

incidents.title: Mass Immigration Arrests at Colorado Springs Underground Nightclub
incidents.summary: Over 300 law enforcement officers from ICE, DEA, and other agencies raided an unlicensed after-hours nightclub called Warike in Colorado Springs, detaining approximately 200 people. More than 100 were placed in ICE custody for immigration violations, while a dozen active-duty military members were among those detained. Despite claims of targeting gang members, no federal or local criminal charges were initially filed.

incidents.title: Judge Orders ICE to Stop Civil Immigration Arrests at Western Slope Courthouses
incidents.summary: Ninth Judicial District Chief Judge John Neiley issued an administrative order directing ICE to cease civil immigration enforcement in and around courthouses in Pitkin, Garfield, and Rio Blanco counties. This was the first judicial use of Colorado's courthouse protection law (SB20-083) since the Trump administration began. The order came after ICE agents maintained a steady presence at the Garfield County Courthouse in Glenwood Springs since January, detaining 5-10 people either inside or just outside the building while perusing court dockets to identify defendants.

incidents.title: Immigrant Rights Activist Jeanette Vizguerra Detained Day After Protest
incidents.summary: Jeanette Vizguerra, a prominent immigrant rights activist named one of Time magazine's 100 most influential people in 2017, was arrested by ICE while on her lunch break at the Target store where she worked. She had spoken out against the Trump administration at a protest at the State Capitol just one day earlier. An ICE officer reportedly said "We finally got you" while arresting her. She was detained for nine months before being released on bond in December 2025.

incidents.title: ICE Detains at Least 3 at Denver Courthouse, Violating State Law
incidents.summary: ICE detained at least three individuals at the Lindsey-Flanigan Courthouse in Denver while they were fulfilling court obligations. One detained man had his 12-year-old son with him, and agents detained the father despite the child not having a guardian present. The Colorado Rapid Response Network confirmed these arrests violated Colorado state law SB20-083, which prohibits civil immigration arrests at courthouses.

incidents.title: At Least Three Detained by ICE After Bonding Out of Routt County Jail
incidents.summary: At least three men were detained by ICE after bonding out of Routt County Jail in early 2025. All were taken to the Denver Contract Detention Facility in Aurora. The detentions included Darwin Mejia-Cruz (27), Victoriano Cayetano Leon (42), and Nelson Martinez Espinoza (44). Mejia-Cruz had prior arrests including allegedly firing a gun in the air nine times at Dream Island mobile home park in Steamboat Springs.

incidents.title: ICE Raids Target Aurora and Denver Apartment Complexes
incidents.summary: Federal agents from ICE, FBI, DEA, and other agencies raided multiple apartment complexes across Aurora and Denver in early morning operations targeting alleged members of the Venezuelan gang Tren de Aragua. The raids displaced families, prevented children from attending school, and sparked controversy over the lack of prior notice to local officials.
incidents.location: Multiple apartment complexes in Aurora and Denver

incidents.title: Hundreds Protest Trump Immigration Actions in Greeley
incidents.summary: Hundreds of people gathered in downtown Greeley to protest Trump administration immigration actions. Protesters marched from Lincoln Park to the Weld County Courthouse, carrying signs condemning mass deportation plans and ICE raids. The protest came amid widespread fear in the community following rumors of raids on the JBS meatpacking plant, which employs a large immigrant workforce. The predominantly Hispanic and Latino crowd came from Greeley and surrounding areas.
incidents.location: Lincoln Park to Weld County Courthouse

incidents.title: Aurora Police and ICE Joint Operation Detains Bystanders in Freezing Temperatures
incidents.summary: Aurora Police Department conducted a joint operation with ICE at The Edge at Lowry apartments, handcuffing all residents present including children as young as 3 and 8 years old. Residents were held outside in 28°F weather in their pajamas from approximately 3:00 AM to 4:30 AM. Children were separated from parents and placed in separate patrol cars. No warrants were shown despite requests. Some people were held for up to 8 hours. The ACLU filed a lawsuit accusing Aurora Police of violating state immigration cooperation laws.
